title: Pairs With a Given Difference

concept.title: Look for two partners
body: Pairs whose values differ by exactly `k` (with `k >= 1`) come in two kinds for a number `x`: the partner is `x - k` or `x + k`. Both are different values, so no pair is counted twice. As before, keep a map of how often each value was seen earlier and add both counts when you read `x`.
For `k = 0` the two partners would be the same value and the formula would count every pair twice, which is why `k` starts at 1 in this problem.

statement: Count the pairs of positions `i < j` in an array of `n` integers for which `|a[i] - a[j]| = k`.

examples.note: Four pairs consist of a 1 and a 3 (two 1s times two 3s), and two pairs consist of a 3 and the 5: six pairs.

hints: For a number `x` the partners are `x - k` and `x + k`.
Use a map with the counts of the numbers read earlier.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

# Your code here

explanation: Every pair is completed by its second number, whose partner is either `x - k` or `x + k`. The counts come from a map of the earlier numbers.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

seen = {}
total = 0
for x in a:
    total += seen.get(x - k, 0) + seen.get(x + k, 0)
    seen[x] = seen.get(x, 0) + 1
print(total)
